tasks.title: Configure Taskmaster to use Claude Code as AI provider
tasks.description: Taskmaster's add-task and other AI-powered commands fail because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and PERPLEXITY_API_KEY are not set. The config.json has an empty claudeCode: {} section that should be configured to route AI generation through the already-authenticated Claude Code CLI (which uses CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) instead of direct API calls. Research how Taskmaster's claudeCode provider integration works, configure it properly, and verify that task-master add-task works without needing separate API keys.

tasks.title: Incorporate Claude Code Agent Teams into Claudio workflow
tasks.description: Research and incorporate Claude Code's official Agent Teams feature (experimental, opt-in via CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1) into the Claudio devcontainer workflow. The codebase already has a custom multi-agent orchestration system using the Task tool (subagents) with coordinator.md, researcher.md, implementer.md, and reviewer.md agents plus the coordinating-agents skill. The official Agent Teams feature adds peer-to-peer messaging between teammates, a shared task list, and self-coordination. Key areas: (1) Enable the feature flag in settings.json, (2) Evaluate adding tmux to the base image for split-pane mode, (3) Determine how team config/task storage in ~/.claude/teams/ and ~/.claude/tasks/ interacts with Claudio's per-container volume strategy, (4) Expand permission pre-approvals to reduce teammate friction, (5) Implement TeammateIdle and TaskCompleted hooks for quality gates, (6) Decide whether to migrate from existing Task tool subagent pattern to official Agent Teams or run both, (7) Update CLAUDE.md and coordinating-agents skill docs.

tasks.title: Implement Taskmaster in the mpulse devcontainer workspace
tasks.description: Initialize Taskmaster in the mpulse workspace (/workspace/mpulse/) by creating .taskmaster/config.json and .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json. The task-master CLI is already available in the container (inherited from the Claudio base image via npm global install), and CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID=mpulse is already set in the container's zshrc. Key decisions: (1) Migrate existing tasks from the manual markdown folder system (tasks/general/, tasks/DPI_Analytics_DBT/, etc.) into Taskmaster's tasks.json format, (2) Decide whether to keep the old tasks/ folder system alongside Taskmaster or deprecate it, (3) Configure .taskmaster/config.json with the claudeCode provider (depends on task #6 being resolved first), (4) Update mpulse/CLAUDE.md to reference Taskmaster workflow instead of/alongside the manual folder-based task lifecycle, (5) Ensure the mpulse orchestration-agent role documented in CLAUDE.md works with Taskmaster's task board.

tasks.title: Fix mpulse devcontainer to build and run again
tasks.description: The mpulse devcontainer fails to start. The container creates successfully but crashes immediately — VS Code gets 'Shell server terminated (code: 1, signal: null)' and 'unable to upgrade to tcp, received 409' when trying to exec into it, meaning the entrypoint is crashing. VS Code also mounts '--mount type=volume,source=vscode,target=/vscode,external=true' which requires a 'vscode' external volume to exist. Known issues to fix: (1) CRITICAL — claudio-shared external volume in docker-compose.yml must exist before compose up or it hard-fails; ensure create-volumes.sh creates it or make it non-external, (2) HIGH — dbt-redshift==1.9.3 may not exist on PyPI, causing the entire pip install layer and image build to fail; verify and pin to an available version or remove if unused, (3) MEDIUM — ${DEV_USER} ARG is used in the mpulse Dockerfile but never declared there (only in the base Dockerfile.base); it expands to empty string causing chown to silently fail with wrong file ownership, (4) LOW — stale comment in docker-entrypoint.sh says the file is not COPY'd into the image but the Dockerfile does COPY and set it as ENTRYPOINT; clean up the contradiction. Fix all issues, verify the image builds successfully, and confirm the container starts and VS Code can attach.

tasks.title: Deploy Claudio container to cloud with remote control access
tasks.description: Set up the Claudio devcontainer to run in the cloud so it can be accessed from anywhere via Claude Code's built-in remote control feature. Key areas: (1) Choose a cloud platform that supports Docker containers with persistent volumes (to preserve Claudio's auth, plugins, and config volume architecture), (2) Deploy the Claudio container (or a cloud-optimized variant) with the necessary volume mounts and environment, (3) Configure Claude Code remote control sessions so the running instance can be connected to from any device, (4) Ensure persistent sessions survive disconnects (tmux, systemd, or similar), (5) Handle authentication and security for remote access, (6) Document the setup and connection workflow.

tasks.title: Research better automated agent orchestration solutions
tasks.description: The current multi-agent setup uses a manual coordinator pattern — a coordinator agent reads the Taskmaster board, dispatches researcher/implementer/reviewer sub-agents via the Task tool, and synthesizes results. This works but requires significant human shepherding. Research more automated orchestration approaches: (1) Evaluate existing frameworks (CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph, OpenAI Swarm, Claude Agent SDK) for orchestrating Claude Code agents with less manual intervention, (2) Investigate whether Claude Code's official Agent Teams feature (task #7) can serve as the orchestration layer with TeammateIdle/TaskCompleted hooks driving automation, (3) Look at CI/CD-style pipelines (GitHub Actions, Dagger) that could trigger agent workflows on events (PR opened, task status changed, etc.), (4) Explore custom orchestrator options — a lightweight daemon or script that watches the Taskmaster board and auto-dispatches agents based on task status, priority, and dependencies, (5) Evaluate tradeoffs: autonomy vs control, cost, token usage, error recovery, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Goal: find or design an orchestration layer that can run the task board with minimal human intervention while maintaining quality gates.

tasks.title: Build Claudio control plane UI for task, agent, and environment management
tasks.description: Design and build a remotely accessible web-based control plane UI for the Claudio platform — accessible from any device/browser over the internet, not just localhost. Core capabilities: (1) TASK MANAGEMENT — full CRUD on tasks with Kanban board, list views, filtering, search, inline editing, comments, and dependency visualization; replace the need to edit tasks.json by hand or use CLI, (2) AGENT MANAGEMENT — view running agents (researchers, implementers, reviewers, agent teams), see their status, logs, and output in real-time; spawn new agents from the UI; kill or redirect agents; assign agents to tasks, (3) ENVIRONMENT MANAGEMENT — view and manage Claudio containers, volumes, and devcontainer configs; start/stop/rebuild containers; view resource usage; manage shared volumes and auth state, (4) GIT WORKTREE SUPPORT — agents working on tasks should operate in isolated git worktrees so they don't conflict with each other or the main working tree; the UI should show active worktrees, which agent owns each, and allow merging results back, (5) SANDBOX / LONG-RUNNING TASKS — support agents running in sandboxed containers on long-running tasks (hours/days); the UI should show progress, allow check-ins, and let you review intermediate output without interrupting the agent; agents should survive disconnects and be reconnectable, (6) REMOTE ACCESS — the UI must be securely accessible over the internet with authentication, not just on localhost; support HTTPS, auth tokens or OAuth, and work from any browser on any device (laptop, phone, tablet). Tech stack TBD but should integrate with Taskmaster's tasks.json format, Claude Code's remote control and Agent Teams features, and Docker for container/worktree orchestration.

tasks.title: Fix Claude credential persistence in mpulse devcontainer
tasks.description: Claude credentials don't survive container rebuilds. Two root causes: (1) claudio-shared volume is declared without external:true in docker-compose.yml, so Docker creates an isolated project-scoped volume instead of using the global shared one from create-volumes.sh — cross-container credential sync never happens. (2) init-claudio's symlink from ~/.claude to ~/.claudio/claude fails silently because the base image creates ~/.claude as a real directory, and the || true swallows the error — credentials go to ephemeral container filesystem. Fix: make claudio-shared external in docker-compose.yml, add ~/.claude symlink setup in entrypoint before init-claudio, log failures instead of swallowing them, add initializeCommand warning in devcontainer.json.

tasks.title: Fix home directory permissions for credential caching
tasks.description: Snowflake CLI (snow) refuses to cache auth tokens because ~/.cache/snowflake/ has 755 permissions instead of required 700. The snow CLI's bundled snowflake-connector-python 3.18.0 has strict FileTokenCache permission validation, while dbt's connector 3.14.0 is lenient. Broader issue: Docker named volumes mount with root:root 755 defaults, WSL bind mounts inherit Windows permissions. Need to audit and fix permissions for all volume-mounted home directories in the entrypoint, with special care for ~/.local/bin executables. Quick fix: add find ~/.cache -type d -exec chmod 700 in entrypoint. Comprehensive fix: expand permission loop for all home subdirectories.
